claimed_purpose.text: MIRIX organizes information into six distinct memory components, each designed to handle specific types of data and provide optimal retrieval performance.
Episodic Memory captures context-specific events and temporal activities, serving as a summarization or calendar of user behaviors.
Core Memory provides persistent information always visible to the agent when interacting with the user.
Multi-agent memory system with six specialized memory components managed by dedicated agents

mechanisms.text: Six distinct memory types are persisted: Core (persona + human profile blocks), Episodic (time-stamped events), Semantic (facts and concepts), Procedural (how-to procedures), Resource (files, links, assets), and Knowledge Vault (sensitive/private facts).

Message history is summarized via an LLM call when the token count of the sequence to summarize exceeds a warning threshold relative to the context window, compressing the log rather than keeping it verbatim.

Context window management summarises history when it reaches 75% of the context window, targets 10% pressure after summarisation, preserves the last 5 messages, prepends the summary, and trims old messages.
The LLM-facing write schema requires occurred_at as a string parseable from the user's response, meaning the LLM is expected to extract event time from conversation content at write time.
Images are handled end-to-end in the memory pipeline: they are converted to ImageContent with an image_id and expanded into real image bytes or URL for provider requests.
Message content types in the memory layer natively support text, image_url, file_uri, and google_cloud_file_uri, but not audio or video as first-class types.
Auto-dream consolidation: reviews existing memories, merges duplicates, resolves stale/conflicting entries, and writes the result back through memory tools
Session conversation store persists message turns including tool calls, tool errors, and assistant responses — full transcript log per session
A transcription helper exists (voice_utils.py) but is not wired into the REST or queue processing path for memory ingestion.
Events are isolated per user, per agent, and per client application, enabling multi-tenant and multi-agent separation.
All memories for a user can be deleted via the users endpoint, and all memories for a client via the clients endpoint.
CoreMemoryAgent is a named agent subclass, implying a dedicated agent role for core memory operations within MIRIX
Async memory extraction is queued via Kafka (aiokafka), decoupling extraction from the synchronous request path.
The mirixAgent class is the entry point for both chat and memory/embedding initialization, configured via YAML.
send_message() is the primary API for processing input into memory, handling classification of what is stored.
Procedural memory migrated to skill-based model; backfill sets scope filter tags per skill's owning client
Memory extraction is gated by a memorizing flag, suggesting extraction is not automatic on every turn
A reflexion_agent performs self-reflection and learning as a distinct agent type.
Foundation of the memory system is derived from the Letta open-source framework
Episodic Memory automatic cleanup archives old entries based on relevance.
MIRIX defines 6 distinct memory types as part of its core architecture
